content:
The image shows a corn ear with:
- Green to gray-green powdery/fuzzy mold growing extensively between and over the kernels
- White mycelium visible at portions of the ear
- The mold covers the ear from middle to tip area, with green-gray conidia prominent
- Yellow kernels still visible beneath/around the mold
- Husks are dry/brown (late season)
- The green coloring is olive to gray-green, not bright green

Key observations:
- Green to gray-green conidia mass covering the ear extensively
- White mycelium also present
- Coverage appears from base/middle up through the ear
- The color is distinctly olive/gray-green, not blue-green (which would suggest Penicillium) and not olive-green powder starting at tip (Aspergillus)

Trichoderma ear rot matches well: "massive production of green to gray-green conidia, often covering the entire ear... white mycelium on husk leaves turning green to gray-green... symptoms typically occurring from base to middle of cob covering all kernels and husk leaf layers."

This fits better than Aspergillus (which is olive-green powder at tip) or Penicillium (blue-green, at tip) or Diplodia (white mycelium from base, no green coloring).

The coverage pattern (mid-ear to tip with white mycelium also present) aligns with Trichoderma rather than Aspergillus (olive-green powder at tip only) or Penicillium (blue-green, tip-focused)."}
